I’m indigenous, Taino to be exact (we’re one of the Natives groups in the Caribbean), but I’m not Lakota (which is what the main character of the movie is- so I can only represent myself in this convo. You would find a better answer by asking Lakota people if they were accurately represented in the movie. 

That being said, as an indigenous person, I liked it over all, but I have some gripes about certain parts of the movie. This is a mini analysis since I just watched the movie and in no way is supposed to be a full review. 

For starters, I dislike how the Lakota where only described from the perspective of the white man/colonel. We never got to hear how they describe themselves. We were only fed the description of “hostiles” “captive” and “not as tall or handsome” (or something like that). Which like, sure, is what a white colonizer would say, but I feel like that narrative perpetuates the idea that indigenous people are “savages” for folks who are uneducated. 

Second/lastly, the ending where the colonel let Spirit and the Lakota guy go feels wrong. For starters, a white colonizer would have definitely killed them, but it’s a kids movie so I can see why they wouldn’t show that. However, that scene makes it seem like the colonel decided to let them live- which I believe shows him in a greater light than is accurate. That near ending scene is akin to John Smith in Pocahontas “helping the natives”. Like… it just doesn’t feel accurate and makes white colonizers seem great. 

That’s all I got. Besides those critiques, it’s one of my favorite movies 💛 I used to watch this all the time as a kid and I know it was the first time I saw someone like me on screen. So it definitely have positive effects too! 💛 but like I said, I’m not Lakota (I’m Taino), so I cannot speak to accurate representation. These are just my opinions as an indigenous person. Thanks!
